offering: Unique Selling Points (for new product line ideas)

productLines.Assist +: Stronger additional offerings for clinician's for a lower price, with tradeoff of not havin dedicated MDS.
productLines.Assist + (w/ integration): Stronger additional offerings for clinician's for a lower price, with tradeoff of not havin dedicated MDS.
productLines.Assist 20 min: Higher cost solution with more a limited scope. Does offer a very requested option of a faster turn around time. There is an efficiency gain for clinicians. Current calculations show that we require a 3:2 or 1.5:1 staffing ratio at this time. This will impact cost of service.
productLines.Assist 20 min + Chart Prep: Higher cost solution with more a limited scope. Does offer a very requested option of a faster turn around time. There is an efficiency gain for clinicians. Current calculations show that we require a 3:2 or 1.5:1 staffing ratio at this time. This will impact cost of service. Pricing also includes the chart prep flat fee.
productLines.Assist Overnight: Notes delievered next day. Lower price tag for similar offering to Assist +. Good option for our Assist clinicians who batch send EOD. Optimizes staffing, but having day shift MDS who receieve all notes from a clinician at one time. Allows clinicians to add additional instructions for the note throughout the day. Allows MDS to be able to use testing results that are made available later in the day.

offering: What needs to be built to support this

productLines.Ambient + Chart Prep: W/o integration, tooling would need to be created in SCP for the chart prep MDS to save the chart prep in SCP. This should allow the carry forward tool to reference it and blend. The clinician would then need to upload the blended note into the EHR themselves.
productLines.Ambient + Chart Prep + Upload: Good option for Ambient + Chart Prep without integration. This could allow for the MDS to paste the blended information in the note for the clinician. Tooling will still need to be created for the carry forward tool as well as an option for the chart prep MDS, to place the chart prep into a field in SCP for the carry forward tool to blend later.
productLines.Ambient + Chart Prep + Integration: Integration and carry forward tooling adjustment will be needed to fully unlock the full potential of the service. Similar tech to carry forward tooling would allow for blending of the chart prep + note from recording. MDS not involved in the actual note blending. MDS will only create the chart prep and add to the EHR. Integration would push the blended note into the EHR.
productLines.Assist Overnight: Similar to queued environment. May require some tweeks to deal with all notes coming in at one time.

offering: Sharing account with multiple clinciains
additionalInfo:
Shared accounts require clinicians to utilize a single device, login, and unified note preferences. Service is exclusive to clinicians successfully onboarded with preference. In the event of overlapping shifts, clinicians must designate a single user for coverage; Commure will not process concurrent recordings or notes. To ensure consistency, all clinicians on a shared account must belong to the same specialty, follow an identical workflow, and utilize a single standardized template.  


Integrated accounts cannot be shared due to possible schedule and documentation cloning.

offering: Ambient Note Upload
additionalInfo:
MDS will place AI note output into the patient's chart. No additional information will be added to the note by the MDS outside of copy/pasting the AI generated note. 

Ambient + Integration: the integration will automatically pull the AI generated note into the patient's note without a human in the loop.

offering: Supporting different clinic types
additionalInfo: Commure can accomodate different clinic types such as Inpatient/outpatient for a single account. In order to support this, we will EHR accounts for both systems (if they are different.) Both clinic types must share the same note style and preferences to maintain consistency.

offering: Scheduling
additionalInfo:
Clinician shares base schedule with Commure during implementation. This information is shared across stakeholders. To update schedule, the clinician must reach out to their CSM/IC/Customer Support. CSM/IC/Customer Support will then inform all internal teams of the schedule change. If the clinician does not share their schedule changes with CSM/IC/Customer Support, Commure cannot guarentee that this schedule change will be accomodating. 

For Live, please note that there is a max number of hours that Commure can require a MDS to work per day. So your primary MDS may not be able to work with you for your entire desired time if it is over 9 hrs.

offering: Customizable Live Note SLA: immediate to next day options
additionalInfo: For Live accounts only. Clinician may share their customized note SLA with Commure. For faster SLAs, precharting/chart prep may be required to meet those SLAs. This means your MDS will start working on your notes before the shift. This may result in an increased cost depending on the extent of precharting/chart prep required to meet the clininician's SLA.

offering: Assist 20 min SLA
additionalInfo:
Notes will be delivered to clinician in the EHR 20 min after the recording is sent to the MDS. Batch sending of notes (more than 1 note at a time, will result in longer SLA.) Autosend feature will be turned on for these accounts automatically to help with meeting this SLA.  3:2 Ratio in queue that only works within a 20 min SLA group. 

To maintain SLA standards- batch sending >2 notes within a 4-minute window will delay the delivery of the 3rd note and any subsequent submissions.It is recommended that clinicians enable the auto-send feature with a customizable interval or frequency. e.g., a clinician can set a 30-minute frequency so that 30 minutes after a visit ends, the note is automatically pushed to MDS if the clinician hasn't sent it manually.

5 is the max number of macros/smartphrases/dotphrases Commure will add per patient/chart (for now)

offering: Assist 60 min Note SLA
additionalInfo: SLA for Assist notes is 60 min starting from the time the recording is sent to Commure.To maintain SLA standards- batch sending >2 notes within a 4-minute window will delay the delivery of the 3rd note and any subsequent submissions.It is recommended that clinicians enable the auto-send feature with a customizable interval or frequency. e.g., a clinician can set a 30-minute frequency so that 30 minutes after a visit ends, the note is automatically pushed to MDS if the clinician hasn't sent it manually. Best practice is to send notes throughout the day and to avoid sending batches of notes. Auto-send option in the Commure App is available to help support this.

offering: Assist 4 hr SLA
additionalInfo:
Notes will be delievered to the clinician in the EHR 4 hrs after the recording is sent to the MDS. If recordings are sent for more than 3 patients at a time, then all patient recordings after the third patient will have a longer SLA. 

in flight case study to see if 4 hours is the right threshold**

offering: Assist Next day SLA
additionalInfo: All recordings and notes sent by 9 pm and notes available at 7 am next day.

offering: Upload Chart Prep information into the patient note
currentState: Timing options available: 1 week in advance, 1 day prior at EOD, Before the Shift, Before the Visit, After the Shift. Some accounts have MDSs update the chart prep based on clinician feedback before the start of the shift.
additionalInfo: Timing options available: 1 week in advance, 1 day prior at EOD, Before the Shift, Before the Visit, After the Shift. For Live Accounts, MDS can update chart prep before the patient's visit based on clinician verbalized instructions.

offering: Gold Standard Templates Only
additionalInfo: On clinician's first day in the app, they will select their specialty and visit types. This will give them gold standard note templates based on their suggestion.

offering: Gold Standard Template + Custom Formatting
additionalInfo: Gold standard template based on specialty and visit types. Template team will then add on custom formatting as needed. For Assist and Live, custom formatting will be applied during ramp up. Adjustments to this custom formatting are done on an as needed basis.

offering: MDS works live on stream with Clinician
additionalInfo:
A MDS is listening/watching a live feed from the provider's device. MDS will following along with provider's work throughout the day. MDS can see both video and audio, clinician can control whether it is both or one. If a clinician is conducting a telehealth visit and using their device to record both patient and clinicient, audio quality will directly impact the ability for Commure to capture details from the visit. If there are key details required for the note, best practice would be to verbalize those details again. 

For Live only, Commure can join Zoom or conference call software to capture note details. No video or audio of MDS will be available for these calls. MDS can listen and see stream only.

offering: Assist: Communication in Commure App
additionalInfo: Message threads between MDSs and Clinician are available for each note. Messaging is available from the time the recording is sent to Commure and ends when the note is uploaded into the EHR. Messaging is available primarily for communication regarding patient notes and EHR workflows.
siteSpecific: Messaging is enabled on a site by site basis.
bestPractices: Goal is not push messaging as a key feature. Move away from this with new sales

offering: Synchronous Communication
additionalInfo: Communication between the clinician and primary MDS is available throughout the scheduled shift. Messages thread is not broken up by note. Clinican may speak to MDS and MDS can communicate back through the app.

offering: Messaging in the EHR
additionalInfo: No across all product lines.

offering: Opening note in the EHR
currentState: Best practice has been to have clinic staff or Clinician open the note. We have accomodating a lot of flexibility with this. Going forward, we will be trying to implement new accounts with having the clinician open the note, except for Live. Live we will continue to allow full flexibility.
additionalInfo:
Commure can either open the note in the EHR or have the clinician/clinic staff open the note. Commure can also accomodate by visit type. This is approved for Live as long as there are no EHR limitations or possible issues. Best practice recommendation is for the clinic staff to open Note. For all product lines outside of Live this is not approved for all new accounts. For all accounts where clinician/clinic staff opens note, not opening the note can result in delayed SLA. 

Outside Live, if clinician requires Commure to open the note we can do that on "exception basis" as long as there is no EHR limitation
siteSpecific: For legacy accounts, we will continue to open notes.
bestPractices: Best practice is that all notes are opened in the same manner.
deviationCausesDelay: yes if the clinician opens the note

offering: Multiple Patients in one recording
additionalInfo:
For Assist, patient recordings must include details for one patient only. 

Exception is made for Pediatricians providers seeing siblings together. Clinician must clearly state which patient they are talking with and which they are giving instructions/dictations for.  

Clinician must limit to max 2 patients per recording under this circumstances; exceeding this limit may result in slower SLA.

offering: Dedicated primary MDS throughout the day
additionalInfo: Clinician will have a dedicated MDS throughout the shift. Some longer shifts may require two MDS split the schedule. This will be decided on a individual basis. All MDS will follow the same set of preferences for the clinician. Commure tries to keep the same MDS on the account as much as possible, but this cannot always be guarenteed. Clinician's preference for MDS will be taken into consideration, however Commure reserves the right to move MDS on and off accounts. Commure will respect clinician's request to remove a MDS from account based off verified professionlism and quality concerns.

offering: Edit EHR templates/dotphrases for grammar or spelling
additionalInfo:
No for all products at this time. Commure will escalate any issues in the templates/macros/dotphrases that become apparent to us through an automated system. Commure does not guarentee they will identify all errors in templates/macros/dotphrases. 

Only available with automated system through customer support.

offering: General Text Formatting: Date Format
currentState: Commure can support these date format options. The clinician's preference will be applied to both note and chart prep if the clinician is receiving both. Options include: Numerical Long Date (MM/DD/YYYY,) Numerical Short Date (M/D/YY,) Numerical without Day (MM, YYYY,) Numerical without Year (DD, YYYY,) and Written Out Format. (Month, Day, Year.)
additionalInfo:
Commure can support these date format options. The clinician's preference will be applied to both note and chart prep if the clinician is receiving both. Options include: Numerical Long Date (MM/DD/YYYY,) Numerical Short Date (M/D/YY,) Numerical without Day (MM, YYYY,) Numerical without Year (DD, YYYY,) and Written Out Format. (Month, Day, Year.) For all product lines outside of Live, Commure will only support one date format for all dates in the notes. Ex, we cannot support one option for HPI and another format for AP section. Any snipped/screenshots will not be formatted to match the clinician's format.

For any ambient + chart prep line, the chart prep will follow the general text formatting options.

offering: General Text Formatting: Medication Format
currentState: Commure can support including a standard set of information for medications in the free text of the note and/or chart prep. The clinician may choose to include any combination of the following pieces of information: Name of medication (choice between all brand names, all generic names, or use the name mentioned in the previous note OR visit discussion,) dosage of medication, frequency of medication, compliance to medication, side effects mentioned by patient during visit or previous clinician's note, and/or recent changes in medication dosage and/or frequency (from last visit.)

offering: Schedule Prep
currentState: Commure will load the clinician's schedule, so that it will be visible in the Commure App. All patients from the clinician's EHR schedule will be added to the Commure App. No same day additions will be added. Commure cannot check the clinician's schedule before the clinician's shift.

Commure can only do Same Day Patient Additions to the schedule with integration. No MDS can update schedule throughout the shift.

offering: Reminders
additionalInfo:

For Assist level products, reminders are only available if engineering tooling is built and clinician also has Chart Prep as a service add on.

offering: Mark note as ready for provider review
additionalInfo: Commure must have correct permissioning to do this. Commure will only do this at the time the note is complete for the clinician. EHR instruction on how mark the note as complete must be shared with Commure.

offering: Chart Prep: Add templates to notes
currentState: Commure will add EHR based template to the note. The templates must be shared with Commure and our operations team. Add "yearlyphysical" template to the note for a patient scheduled for their annual physical.

these will not be verbatim transcription. AI will refine the content for proper grammar and professional phrasing while maintaining the clinician's intent. If clinician requires their dictation verbatim, shorter SLA 20 min cannot be supported

5 is the max number of macros/smartphrases/dotphrases Commure will add per patient/chart (for now) for Assist 20 min

offering: Select answers options in smarttext (EPIC)
additionalInfo:
Commure can select options in SmartText sections. SmartText dotphrases must be shared with Commure. All information necessary to select options in the SmartText need to be made available to the MDS using the visit discussion or clinician verbalization. 

15 is the max number of macros/smartphrases/dotphrases Commure will add per patient/chart (for now) for all Assist product line but Assist 20 min 

5 is the max number of macros/smartphrases/dotphrases Commure will add per patient/chart (for now) for Assist 20 min

offering: Assessment and Plan
currentState: Commure can organize the AP details in the note. Commure can add information into the AP based on visit discussion and clinician verbalization. Commure can add additional details to testing results and medications based on clinician's chosen formatting options. Commure can find missing details to the testing results and medication details in the patient chart. Commure can also add details based on orders placed in the EHR.
additionalInfo:
Commure can organize the AP details in the note. Commure can add information into the AP based on visit discussion and clinician verbalization. Commure can add additional details to testing results and medications based on clinician's chosen formatting options. Commure can find missing details to the testing results and medication details in the patient chart. Commure can also add details based on orders placed in the EHR.  Commure can organize the AP based on assessments/diagnosis discussed during the visit or verbalized by the clinician. Commure does not support adding AP details for a diagnosis that was not dicussed with patient during the visit, but Commure can copy forward the AP details for that diagnosis from the clinician's last note OR add details based on clinician dictation.  

For Assist product lines, the orders included in the AP must be placed at the time of the recording is sent to Commure.

offering: Regenerating the note with a different commure template
additionalInfo: No across all product lines (for now.) We do not have the tooling built for this. If this feature can be given to our MDS, we can offer this across all product lines.

offering: Add testing results available after the visit.
additionalInfo: Commure can add additional testing results that will be available after the visit as directed by the clinician. The clinician must dictate at the end of the recording or message MDS in the Commure App. If dictating at the end of the recording, all dictations must begin with "start dictation" and end with "end dictation." Clinician should indicate what testing result they would like added to the note. This is only available for Live. This is not available for assist.

offering: Adding additional information to note after note upload
additionalInfo: Commure can make additions or changes to the patient note after the MDS has saved the note in the EHR. MDS must have correct permissioning to do this and the updates must be directed clearly by the provider. The note should not be signed by the provider yet.

offering: Forward Notes
additionalInfo: Commure can add verbalized clinician names for note forwarding and copy forward the list of clinicians who should receive the note. Clinician must dictate the clinician's name with spelling for the note to be forwarded. If note is being forwarded to the referring clinician, the referring clinician's name must be accessible in the previous note.

offering: CSS: Pend Orders (Imaging, Labs, Referrals)
additionalInfo:
Commure can pend/purpose orders in the EHR for the clinician. Clinician must verbalize all details needed to pend/purpose the order. The clinician must have a sign off step before the order is officially sent in for the patient. If the clinician has favorites or panels of orders, Commure can use these as long as they are shared. 


AVS, Pend Orders, Referral Letters, Prior Authorization, Coding, Forward Notes, AVS etc~ Currently, these are viewed as additional deliverables/ CSS including for Live- will this not be the future state?

For Live services, clinicians are capped at 2-3 CSS items; any requirements exceeding this limit will incur additional charges.

offering: CSS: Referral Letters
additionalInfo:
Commure can fill in referral letter main text area and department/clinician name. Clinician must verbalize clinician name or department information required to send the letter. Clinician must share any dotphrases needed if they would like them used in the referral letter. Context of referral letter must be either produced using a dotphrase or verbalized by the clinician. 

For Live services, clinicians are capped at 2-3 CSS items; any requirements exceeding this limit will incur additional charges.

offering: Ped Medications or Vaccinations
additionalInfo: No across all product lines

offering: CSS: Discrete data entry of past medical history
additionalInfo: Commure can enter past medical history details into patient chart. The details that are needed to update the patient chart must be dictated/verbalized by the clinician.

offering: CSS: Discrete data entry of surgical history
additionalInfo: Commure can enter social history details into patient chart. The details that are needed to update the patient chart must be dictated/verbalized by the clinician. Best practice would be to have Commure do this for specific visit types or do only when directed by the clinician.
bestPractices: Best practice would be to have Commure do this for specific visit types or do only when directed by the clinician.

offering: CSS: Discrete data entry of family medical history
additionalInfo: Commure can enter family medical history details into patient chart. The details that are needed to update the patient chart must be dictated/verbalized by the clinician.
bestPractices: Best practice would be to have Commure do this for specific visit types or do only when directed by the clinician.

offering: CSS: Discrete data entry update problem list
additionalInfo: Commure can enter problem list details into patient chart. The details that are needed to update the patient chart must be dictated/verbalized by the clinician.
bestPractices: Best practice would be to have Commure do this for specific visit types or do only when directed by the clinician.

offering: CSS: After Visit Summaries
additionalInfo:
Commure can add after visit summaries to the patient's chart. The contents of the AVS should be either verbalized by the clinician or be an easy to follow rule. Example, copy Assessment and Plan into AVS free text area for all visits. Commure can also place dotphrases into AVS free text areas, but these dotphrases need to be shared with Commure. Dotphrases should either be verbalized by clinician OR placed using easy to follow rules based on visit type or complaint. 

For Assist, After Visit Summaries will follow the same SLA as the note itself and will not be available immediately at the end of the visit.

offering: CSS: Patient Instructions
additionalInfo:
Commure can add patient instructions to the patient's chart. The contents of the patient instructions should be either verbalized by the clinician or be an easy to follow rule. Example, copy Assessment and Plan into patient instruction free text area for all visits. Commure can also place dotphrases into patient instruction free text areas, but these dotphrases need to be shared with Commure. Dotphrases should either be verbalized by clinician OR placed using easy to follow rules based on visit type or complaint.

For Assist, After Visit Summaries will follow the same SLA as the note itself and will not be available immediately at the end of the visit.

offering: CSS: Track and Note visit duration time
currentState: Commure can add a statement regarding how much time was spent with a patient. The time can be verbalized by clinician OR Commure can use visit recording length as the time spent with patient.
additionalInfo:
Commure can add a statement regarding how much time was spent with a patient. The time can be verbalized by clinician OR Commure can use visit recording length as the time spent with patient. 
For Live, commure can enter the time into a discrete data field.  
For Assist, clinician must dictate the amount of time spent with the patient. 
Regardless of product line, if two or more patients were seen during one recording the clinician must dictate the time spent with each patient. If this information is not dictated, no statement will be entered into the note.

offering: CSS: Discrete data entry medication details
additionalInfo: Commure can enter medication details into patient chart. The details that are needed to update the patient chart must be dictated/verbalized by the clinician.
bestPractices: Best practice would be to have Commure do this for specific visit types or do only when directed by the clinician.

offering: CSS: Prior Authorization
additionalInfo: Commure will add specific prior authorization details to the patient’s note when verbalized by the clinician. The details of the prior authorization must be dictated by the provider. Commure will only add statements into the patient's note at this time. Commure will add a dotphrase and add dictations as given by provider. Dictations must be given at the end of the recording, dictations must be queued with "start dictation" and end with "end dictation'
siteSpecific: UCSF clinicians also have the option of including screenshot/snip of specific portions of the imaging report added to the note. The rules for when to use a screenshot/snip must be easily followed based on imaging result type, patient condition, or visit type. any additional information needed to fill in blanks in the dotphrase text need to be dictated with a "start dictation" and "end dictation pattern.

offering: CSS: Coding
currentState: Commure will add billing and diagnostic codes to the patient visit only when verbalized by the clinician. This includes ICD-10, E&M, LOS, CPT, and HCC codes.(Note, best practice and intial roll out of coding required clinician to dictate the codes. Some accounts have drifted from this standard.)
additionalInfo:
Commure will add billing and diagnostic codes to the patient visit only when verbalized by the clinician. This includes ICD-10, E&M, LOS, CPT, and HCC codes. Clinician must dictate all coding details for these to be placed. If the clinician does not dictate the codes, then commure will not add them to the note/patient visit. Codes will be entered exactly as dictated.  

For Assist, Coding can be provided with integration as long as no MDS time is required to accomplish the coding.

For Live services, clinicians are capped at 2-3 CSS items; any requirements exceeding this limit will incur additional charges.

offering: Autocoding
additionalInfo: For Ambient only,  ICD and E/M codes are AI generated and available in SuperApp.

offering: Image Assist
additionalInfo: Commure will add text to images uploaded by clinician into the note. Clinician must verbalize what information needs to be included. Best practice is to verbalize information as it should appear in the note.

offering: CSS: Updating note status in EHR
additionalInfo: Commure will update note status in the EHR. We will change the status of the visit based off clinician guidance or when the clinician leaves the patient room. The only option we can support is changing the status when the note is complete.

offering: CSS: Discrete Data Entry follow up instructions
additionalInfo: Commure will add follow up details to the Wrap Up section of the note. The follow up instructions must be verbalized by clinician and entered into discrete boxes. Commure will add timeline of when to follow up. The follow up instructions can also be placed in the note itself.
